engine: 11tanjung's signature reveal — N outline circles sit in a row (overlapping = a venn). On a pinned scroll-scrub the SIDE circles do a stroke-width radial fill (thin ring -> solid disc) then hollow + shrink to a dot and drift toward the edges, while the CENTRE circle becomes a clip-path: circle(r) mask on a full-bleed render whose radius scrubs 0% -> ~85% (covers the viewport); the render counter-scales 1.15 -> 1 as the portal opens; the venn labels fade out. Harvested from D_11tanjung (C1; b024 thin rings -> b028 side discs filled -> b033 side dots + centre portal opening -> b048 full render).

measured_teardown.move: ONE pinned scroll-scrub, progress p 0..1. Side rings: 0..fillEnd(0.4) the border-width grows 1px -> ~61px (a thin ring fills into a solid disc); fillEnd..1 the border hollows back to 1px while the disc shrinks (scale -> 0.06) and drifts outward (translateX along its resting offset), opacity easing down. Centre: the RENDER is masked by clip-path: circle(0% -> 85% at 50% 50%) growing from the centre, + render transform scale 1.15 -> 1 (counter-scale). The centre 'portal' ring is a thin transparent guide that fades over the first 60%. Labels (/01 /02 /03 + caption) fade over the first 50%. ease power2.out on every channel.
measured_teardown.cited: 11tanjung C1 b024 (three thin outline rings, closed) -> b028 (side rings filled to discs) -> b033 (side rings hollowing + shrinking to dots, centre portal opening onto the render) -> b048 (centre portal full, render full-bleed, side rings gone).

rings.what: number of circles in the row; the centre one (.vrp-ring--portal) is the portal mask, the rest are the side rings. Odd counts keep one centred.

fillEnd.what: progress at which the side rings finish filling into discs and begin to hollow + shrink + drift. Before it = fill; after it = collapse.

pinFactor.what: length of the pinned scroll span (end = +innerHeight*pinFactor). Higher = slower, longer reveal.

ease.what: the scrub curve applied to fill, hollow, shrink, drift and the portal radius. power2.out = fast open, settling tail (the 11tanjung curve). 'expo.out' available for a harder snap.

manageLenis.what: if true and Lenis is present, the component owns a Lenis instance + ticker; set false when the page already drives a shared Lenis (lab sets false).

entry: VennRingPortalReveal.create(target, opts) -> { trigger, lenis, set(p), refresh(), destroy }. target = .vrp-stage wrapping .vrp-render(img) + .vrp-rings(.vrp-ring x N, centre = .vrp-ring--portal) + optional .vrp-labels. set(p 0..1) is a PURE scrub (0 = three thin closed rings, no render; 1 = portal full, render revealed).
law: clip-path: circle (the centre, on the render) + border-width (side rings fill) + transform scale/translateX (shrink + drift, render counter-scale) + opacity only; GPU; NO mix-blend / NO backdrop over the scrubbed render; NO WebGL; reduced-motion or <=820px -> portal open (render shown), no pin. owns_pin TRUE (the move IS the pinned scroll). GSAP + ScrollTrigger required for the scroll path; set(p) works standalone for previews/snapshots.
gate_mode: owns_pin scroll-scrub. clip-path/SVG-style media -> a naive blank% probe is a FALSE blank at p<1; verify the portal-radius + side-border curve and fps/jank directly, NOT blank%. Drive the LAB's own pinned instance (scroll to p*innerHeight*pinFactor); do NOT create() a second instance to screenshot (two pins on one element conflict).
proven: lab: OUR QUADRO render (terrace.webp) behind three rings. Curve measured live (p / clip-radius / side-border / render-scale): 0 / 0% / 1px / 1.15 -> 0.2 / 30.6% / 31px / 1.096 -> 0.36 / 50.2% / 55px / 1.061 -> 0.62 / 72.7% / 25px / 1.022 -> 0.78 / 80.9% / 9px / 1.007 -> 0.85 / 83.1% / 4px / 1.003 -> 1 / 85% / 1px / 1. Side border peaks ~55px near fillEnd then hollows back to 1px while the disc shrinks + drifts out. Mid-portal frame (p=0.62) = the QUADRO building revealed through a centre circle, two hollow side rings (/01 /03), warm-brown fields, '11 tanjung' pill top-centre (matches 11tanjung b033). Probe (4x CPU throttle): 1/682 long frames (0.1%), 59.9fps -> PASS.
